relation_proposals.evidence_context: Evaluation must distinguish the quality of retrieval from the quality of the generated answer. Retrieval recall measures how many relevant passages the search returns, while retrieval precision measures how many returned passages are relevant. Neither measure alone shows whether the tutor uses the retrieved evidence correctly. An answer can cite a real passage while making a claim that the passage does not support. The tutor is therefore evaluated for factual correctness, support from the supplied documents, and appropriate handling of uncertainty. When two course passages disagree, the tutor should identify the disagreement rather than combine them into an unsupported conclusion. A failure to retrieve supporting evidence means that support was not found; it does not prove that the proposed claim is false.
